recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any reconsideration of similar wording in AuditEvent should be handled as a separate Security WG issue rather than expanding this Provenance decision.
issue_request: FHIR-55409 was Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core Provenance. It requested changing the Provenance W3C Entity bullet from entities MAY be real or imaginary to entities might be physical or virtual/electronic, avoiding misleading Provenance semantics and non-conformance use of MAY.
initial_application: Jira linked HL7/fhir#4066. Git commit 5e322f3f2f changed source/provenance/provenance-introduction.xml so the Entity bullet uses physical or virtual/electronic wording and the adjacent Agent bullet uses might instead of MAY.
additional_context: The issue was discovered while investigating the same Provenance W3C model paragraph and PR as FHIR-55410. source/fhir.ini lists provenance=Provenance. A broader source search found older similar W3C wording in AuditEvent, but FHIR-55409 is scoped to FHIR-core Provenance and PR #4066 did not apply it to AuditEvent.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Provenance narrative source already reflects the applied Jira request, so an empty no-change audit commit was published.

related_jiras.note: Same PR and Provenance W3C model paragraph; FHIR-55410 needed the ElementDefinition and mapping exception reconciliation in this run.
